content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee: Keith Mclaughlin (E032) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two conflicting notes:
- Note 1 (HR?): says full-time Analyst, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (Security): says contractor with basic security training, recommendation read.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write, admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns it). So full-time Analyst max = write.
- contractor: read, or write only with advanced security training. Never admin. This contractor has basic training, so max = read.

The conflicting facts: one says full-time, one says contractor with basic training. The Security DB note appears to be a correction ("not full-time as previously noted"). The recommendation from security is read.

Given the conflicting info, which to trust? The Security agent claims the DB shows contractor with basic security training. This seems like a correction. The approver should consider the most accurate/current info. The security note explicitly says the previous note was incorrect.

So max access = read (contractor with basic training). Requested write > read, so grant maximum = read.

I'll submit decision: read.
